newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Hyal says parent wants new board.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Hyal says parent wants new board.

text.p: Hyal Pharmaceuticals Australia Ltd (HPAL) said on Tuesday its parent Hyal Pharmaceutical Corp (HPC) proposes to call an extraordinary shareholders meeting to consider the removal of the Australian company's board.
The Australian company said HPC aimed to remove all directors of HPAL with the exception of Sam Asculai, the chief executive of Toronto, Canada-based HPC.
HPC owns 60 percent of HPAL, whose shares were suspended on the Australian Stock Exchange earlier in the day.

The Australian company uses HPC drug delivery technology but The Australian newspaper reported on Tuesday that HPAL was unhappy that improvements it had made to the technology remained property of the parent and that there were suggestions it wanted to go its own way.

A letter from HPC's lawyers released by HPAL said the Australian company had declined to appoint HPC-nominated replacements for two of HPC's three board representatives who stepped down for personal reasons about one year ago.

The letter also expressed concern about ongoing operations of the Australian subsidiary including standards of servicing, dwindling employee resources, lack of management focus and quality of information on which decisions were being made.

"Following certain decisions taken by the Hyal Australia board ... Hyal considers it needs to take urgent action to normalise and improve the functioning and operations of Hyal Australia's board and management," the letter said.
The letter said Tony Hartnell, a partner in the law firm, Atanaskovic Hartnell, had agreed to stand as a new independent director and if elected would become new chairman of HPAL.
Hartnell is former chairman of The Australian Securities Commission.
HPAL shares fell one cent to 39 cents on Monday, the last day they traded before being suspended.
